newsitem.title: UK: UK shares end mixed, currency and politics weigh.
newsitem.headline: UK shares end mixed, currency and politics weigh.

text.p: ** UK's FTSE 100 index ends modestly higher on the back of
a late surge in B.A.T, which adds 5 pts to index.
** B.A.T climbs on hopes for U.S. tobacco settlement.
** Volumes stay thin. Rate worries, sterling, tax concerns
weigh on sentiment. Dow recovers opening losses.

B.A.T added five points to the leading index after finishing 30-1/2p higher at 543-1/2p. The shares rose on fresh hopes of a settlement to U.S. tobacco-related legal claims and were also helped by strong first quarter profits from U.S. tobacco giant Philip Morris.
Turnover in B.A.T shares was a hefty 12.5 million shares. But overall advancers and decliners were roughly evenly matched.
Mid-250 stocks were left behind as the index edged up 2.9 points to 4,524.6.
UK stocks had pushed cautiously higher at the start of trade following the Dow's 135-point advance overnight.
But trading volumes remained light and gains were capped as domestic concerns kept activity to a minimum.
Fears that the opposition Labour Party, the clear favourites to win the May 1 election, would need to raise corporate taxes to shore up fragile government finances were cited as a concern.
Analysts were also worried that Labour may agree to a 50 basis point interest rate rise shortly after the election, to establish credibility with the financial markets.
Institutional investors shied away and sterling-related profit warnings from Reuters and Reed helped to depress market sentiment and drag shares to session lows.

Reuters recovered to finish just 1/2p lower at 591-1/2p, after the company said that if the pound remained at current levels it expects to announce little or no growth in pre-tax profit and earnings at the half-year stage.
Anglo-Dutch publisher Reed Elsevier ended 6-1/2p higher at 11.00 stg despite warning that the currency's strength would have a "marked effect" on its first half results.

"The worries that people have are over the impact of strong sterling as well as the outlook for interest rates," said a trader. "There is a lot of uncertainty but there is also a lot of cash, so we are just stuck in the middle."

News that UK unemployment fell by 41,000 in March and that average earnings rose in line with expectations had little impact on prices but Bank of America economist Jeremy Hawkins said "the UK data should at least be enough to keep speculation about a post-election tightening of 25 basis points."

Stronger-than-expected industrial output data from the U.S. finally led UK stocks into reverse but the Dow later recovered from its weaker opening to be up 10 points as London markets closed. Gilts finished slightly lower ahead of key UK inflation data on Thursday.
